text: pharmr.extra R package extends pharmr — R bindings Python’s Pharmpy PK modeling library — higher-level utilities bug workarounds. Key entry points: - create_model() — Builds Pharmpy model object (main heavy function R/create_model.R) - run_nlme() — Fits model (preferred deprecated fit_model()) - run_sim() / run_simulation() — Simulation utilities Pharmpy API compatibility: Several functions handle differences pharmpy v1.x v2.0+ (e.g., set_dv.R uses ColumnInfo type detection). touching dataset/datainfo manipulation, check API paths. Known bug workarounds: R/read_modelfit_results.R overrides pharmr::read_modelfit_results() fixes SAEM+IMP multi-step estimation failures. See memory file details four bugs patched . R/patch_pharmpy_nlmixr.R monkey-patches Pharmpy’s nlmixr backend (pharmpy.tools.external.nlmixr.run) bootstrap/modelsearch search tools work nlmixr2 models; call_pharmpy_tool() applies automatically nlmixr-format models.

title: SIR covariance estimation in NONMEM
text: Sampling Importance Resampling (SIR) method estimating parameter uncertainty NONMEM (7.3+) can run part $COVARIANCE step. works : Sampling parameter vectors proposal distribution (typically asymptotic normal distribution centered FOCE estimates, covariance matrix variance). Weighting sample well matches observed data relative proposal distribution. Resampling replacement according weights, yielding set parameter draws approximate true posterior. output set weighted parameter vectors rather single covariance matrix, makes SIR robust standard covariance step : dataset small asymptotic covariance matrix unreliable. model highly nonlinear parameter distributions skewed. standard covariance step fails (e.g., non-positive-definite R matrix). full multivariate uncertainty distribution needed simulation. SIR slower standard covariance step much faster nonparametric bootstrap, produces uncertainty estimates closely match likelihood profiling practice (Dosne et al., 2016, doi:10.1007/s10928-016-9487-8).

title: SIR covariance estimation in NONMEM
text: Three plots lst-file output help assess SIR quality: dOFV distribution — distribution dOFV = OFV(sample) - OFV(FOCE) values SIR samples follow chi-squared distribution. distribution shifted right, proposal narrow; increase SIRSAMPLE. Spatial trends — scatter plot importance ratios vs. individual parameters. flat (horizontal) trend indicates good proposal match. bell-shaped trend means proposal wide; U-shaped trend means narrow. Temporal trends — importance ratio vs. sample index. flat trend indicates good samples depleted. trend drifts iterations, increase SIRSAMPLE SIRNITER.

Default 1, .e. peripheral distributions. elimination elimination type, either linear michaelis-menten. iiv either character list object. character, either "basic" (CL V parameters) "" (IIV parameters). specified list object, contain IIV magnitude (SD scale) parameters potential correlations specified using tilde, e.g. list("CL" = 0.2, "V" = 0.3, "CL~V" = 0.1). iiv_type either character list. character, one c("exp", "add", "prop", "log", "re_log"). list, specify parameter effect type, e.g. list(CL = "add", V = "exp"). Default "exp" . tmdd_type TMDD model structure desired, can choose one full, ib, crib, cr, qss, mmapp. See Pharmpy/pharmr documentation details. metabolite either TRUE/FALSE list. logical, determines metabolite compartment added (input central using linear kinetics). case, DVID dataset set 1 parent compound 2 metabolite. argument list object, require list elements dvid_drug (integer) presystemic (logical) specified. dvid_drug specified index number parent drug DVID column dataset. presystemic determines whether metabolite formed absorption (TRUE), systemic absorption (FALSE). ruv one proportional, additive, combined. force_ode force creation model ODEs, even though model linear. Available methods: "fo", "foce", "", "impmap", "imp", "saem". estimation_options options estimation method(s). single estimation method, specify flat list, e.g. list(NITER = 50). multiple estimation methods, specify named list lists names match method names, e.g. list(SAEM = list(NBURN = 500), IMP = list(NITER = 10)). Methods listed use default options. flat list provided multiple estimation methods, applies first step . uncertainty_method Compute uncertainty parameter estimations. Available options m1, m3, m4, m5, m6, m7, described Beal et al. Columns renamed passed pharmpy $INPUT uses standard names. Uses parse_data_dictionary() defaults names specified. mu_reference Control mu-referencing model.
